pr_title: core: do not reset tty if there's no tty configured
pr_body:
Otherwise a lock is taken, which can be taken by multiple units at the same time, depending on each other, causing a deadlock.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/29682
pr_comments: @mrc0mmand does this help with the efi.mount race?

> @mrc0mmand does this help with the efi.mount race?

I have it running for 30+ minutes in a loop and so far it hasn't failed once, so I'd say this indeed helps.

Sanitizers seem to be unhappy:

```
../build/src/basic/terminal-util.c:333:27: runtime error: null pointer passed as argument 1, which is declared to never be null
/usr/include/fcntl.h:213:6: note: nonnull attribute specified here
```

issue_context.title: Intermittent timeouts when starting efi.mount during boot

Which confirms that https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/af189d7b50823876e71d1be5f5c575281ffb99c7 is the culprit, as the process gets stuck when taking the /dev/console lock.
I guess that systemd-vconsole-setup.service takes the /dev/console lock and then waits for efi.mount (systemd-boot-update.service), which also wants the lock, hence the deadlock.
but hmm, why would efi.mount want the lock?
We take the lock in the sd-executor stuff in `exec_invoke()` through `exec_context_tty_reset()` when executing mount.
